Eight occurrences of the bare name were read as the patriarch, overturned by an audit that named the tribe instead, and refused by the loader because writing a person called the tribe of Benjamin would have been a falsehood of our own making. Every πνεῦμα within three words of ἅγιος names it: 365 words of the four Greek editions in 94 verses, the Textus Receptus adding JHN 7:39, ACT 6:3, 8:18, 1CO 2:13 and 1JN 5:7. Of the 121 standing beside θεός, the verses that say the Spirit of God are linked; God is a Spirit (JHN 4:24), the spirit of slumber (ROM 11:8), the Spirit of his Son (GAL 4:6), a habitation of God through the Spirit (EPH 2:22), PHP 3:3, where the editions read it apart, the spirit of fear (2TI 1:7), the spirits of just men (HEB 12:23), 1PE 4:6, every spirit that confesseth (1JN 4:2#2) and the seven Spirits of God and the God of the spirits of the prophets in Revelation are not. The Spirit without an epithet is linked only where the same verse or passage names it: the dove at the baptism (MRK 1:10; JHN 1:32-33), the leading into the wilderness (MAT 4:1; MRK 1:12; LUK 4:1), the utterance at Pentecost (ACT 2:4), 1CO 2:10, and in Romans 8, after 8:9 and 8:11 call it the Spirit of God, the verses where both the King James and Nestle's edition print it as the Spirit (8:2, 9, 11, 14, 16, 23, 26, 27); 8:4-6, 8:10, 8:13 and 8:15, which the two read apart, are left. In the Hebrew Bible only holy spirit is linked (PSA 51:11; ISA 63:10-11).
